newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI chairman sees rupee stable in near term.
newsitem.headline: India SBI chairman sees rupee stable in near term.

text.p: The chairman of State Bank of India (SBI), India's largest commercial bank, said on Monday he expected the rupee to be stable over the next two to three months.
"I personally think the rupee would remain at current levels over the next two to three months," SBI chairman Pandurang Kakodkar told Reuters in an interview.
Kakodkar said SBI was currently processing applications for dollar-denominated loans out of its FCNR(B) (foreign currency non-resident) deposits maintained by expatriate Indians.
These applications were worth between $50.0 million to $60.0 million, he said.
The bank was processing applications of only those Indian firms which had income streams in foreign exchange, he said.
The rupee was quoted at 35.89/90 in latest deals on Monday, after opening at 35.92/93, dealers said.
